summary: Executed backend + frontend regression for Azure single-container deployment contract on preview URL. SPA/static serving, health behaviors, auth/CORS/lockout checks, upload validations, deployment-file contract checks, production frontend build, and core UI navigation/login/logout were validated.

critical.issue: Authenticated screenshot response cache-control header observed as 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' instead of expected strict 'private, no-store'.

action_items: Confirm where Cache-Control is being rewritten for admin screenshot responses (app vs ingress/proxy/CDN) and enforce required 'private, no-store'.
If strict header contract is required at edge, add/verify response header passthrough policy to preserve private directive.
Optional test hygiene: provide /app/tmp/pre-rotation-admin-token.txt fixture when validating token-rotation negative-path tests.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/lib/uploads.py uses a fallback default path when UPLOAD_DIR is unset; if fail-fast env-only policy is mandatory, this should be tightened.
Server route logic correctly keeps unknown /api/* routes out of SPA fallback and preserves JSON 404 behavior.
Admin duplicate-warning Mongo queries are correctly bounded with limit(10) in backend/routers/admin.py.
seed_data_creation: Yes. Regression tests created TEST_* registrations via /api/registration/submit during execution.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Current blocker is only screenshot cache-control contract mismatch on authenticated image endpoint. All other requested Azure/container/static/health/auth/UI checks passed in this run. Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_azure_deployment_contract.py::test_authenticated_screenshot_endpoint_is_private_no_store after header-policy fix.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: login as admin, list registrations, open /api/admin/registrations/{id}/screenshot, inspect response headers. Observed cache-control includes no-store/no-cache/must-revalidate but missing explicit private token expected by requirement. Code in backend/routers/admin.py sets 'private, no-store', so likely override/normalization occurs in middleware/proxy/CDN layer. Mitigation: enforce final edge response header policy or ensure upstream header is preserved exactly.
